entries.title: Defer feature updates by 30 days
entries.description: Holds new Windows feature (annual) updates for 30 days after Microsoft releases them, so early-rollout issues surface before the update reaches this device.
entries.rationale: Feature updates are not security updates, so a short deferral costs nothing on the security side while avoiding day-one regressions. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education; best-effort and unverified on Home.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select when Preview builds and Feature Updates are received

entries.title: Defer feature updates by 90 days
entries.description: Holds new Windows feature (annual) updates for 90 days after Microsoft releases them.
entries.rationale: A quarter's deferral lets a feature release mature before it reaches this device without withholding any security patches. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education; best-effort and unverified on Home.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select when Preview builds and Feature Updates are received

entries.title: Defer feature updates by 180 days
entries.description: Holds new Windows feature (annual) updates for 180 days after Microsoft releases them.
entries.rationale: A long deferral keeps the device on the mature previous release for half a year. Combined with the annual cadence it can leave the device a full version behind, so it is a Strict-level choice. Security (quality) updates are unaffected.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select when Preview builds and Feature Updates are received

sideEffects: The device can stay a full Windows version behind the current release; ensure the running version does not reach end-of-servicing during the deferral window.

entries.title: Defer feature updates by 365 days
entries.description: Holds new Windows feature (annual) updates for the maximum 365 days after Microsoft releases them.
entries.rationale: The maximum supported feature deferral effectively skips a yearly release. Security (quality) updates still arrive, but the device must not be left on a release that reaches end-of-servicing during the window.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select when Preview builds and Feature Updates are received

sideEffects: The device can stay a full Windows version behind; the end-of-servicing warning must be heeded before the running release lapses.

entries.title: Defer quality (security) updates by 7 days
entries.description: Holds the monthly quality (security) updates for 7 days after Microsoft releases them, so widespread install problems are known before this device patches.
entries.rationale: A short quality deferral is a deliberate stability-over-immediacy trade for people who would rather wait a week than be first. It delays security fixes, so it is Advanced risk and Strict level; the maximum supported value is 30 days.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select when Quality Updates are received

sideEffects: Security updates are withheld for 7 days after release, leaving already-fixed vulnerabilities exposed on this device during that window.

entries.title: Pin the feature release to 25H2
entries.description: Keeps the device on Windows 11 25H2 (sets the TargetReleaseVersion trio) so it is not offered a newer feature release until 25H2 reaches end of servicing.
entries.rationale: Pinning a specific supported release gives a stable, known platform. Both TargetReleaseVersionInfo and ProductVersion must be set for the pin to be honoured; the pin expires at end-of-servicing and the device is then offered the newest applicable release.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Select the target Feature Update version

sideEffects: The device stays on 25H2 and is not offered a newer feature release until 25H2 reaches end of servicing; check 'otw updates status' for the days remaining.

entries.title: Keep off-by-default new features off
entries.description: Turns on Temporary Enterprise Feature Control so features that ship disabled inside monthly cumulative updates stay off until a full feature update enables them.
entries.rationale: Avoids surprise mid-cycle behaviour changes on a managed device; the feature set only moves when the annual feature update lands. Documented for Windows 11 22H2 and later.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Enable features introduced via servicing that are off by default

entries.title: Notify before installing updates
entries.description: Configures Automatic Updates so updates download automatically but Windows notifies you before installing them, letting you choose when the install and restart happen.
entries.rationale: Keeps patches downloading in the background while giving control over the disruptive install/restart step. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education; honoured on Home only best-effort.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Configure Automatic Updates

sideEffects: Installs wait for you to act, so a patch can sit un-installed if you keep dismissing the notification; add a compliance deadline if you need guaranteed patching.

entries.title: Delivery Optimization: no peer sharing (HTTP only)
entries.description: Sets Delivery Optimization download mode to HTTP only (0), so update content comes only from Microsoft and is never shared with or from other devices.
entries.rationale: The documented way to turn off peer-to-peer update sharing entirely — no LAN or internet peers — for privacy and predictable bandwidth. Windows Update itself is unaffected.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Delivery Optimization\Download Mode

entries.title: Delivery Optimization: simple mode (no cloud service)
entries.description: Sets Delivery Optimization download mode to Simple (99) so it uses neither peers nor the Delivery Optimization cloud service — updates download directly from Microsoft.
entries.rationale: For isolated or privacy-sensitive networks that want no contact with the Delivery Optimization cloud metadata service at all. Nothing breaks, but Microsoft Connected Cache and peer acceleration are lost.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Delivery Optimization\Download Mode

sideEffects: Delivery Optimization's cloud service, peer sharing and Microsoft Connected Cache are all disabled, so large updates download directly and can be slower.

entries.title: Don't send malware-removal infection reports
entries.description: Stops the monthly Malicious Software Removal Tool from sending infection details to Microsoft. The tool still runs and cleans; only the report is suppressed.
entries.rationale: Removes a telemetry flow without weakening protection — the MSRT is not an antivirus and Microsoft Defender covers the same malware families continuously.

entries.title: Turn off Microsoft Store app auto-updates
entries.description: Sets the Microsoft Store policy so apps are not downloaded and installed automatically. You update Store apps manually from the Store's Library page.
entries.rationale: Gives control over when Store apps change. It is a deliberate trade-off: Store apps stop patching themselves, so it is Advanced risk and Strict level, and you must remember to update them.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Store\Turn off Automatic Download and Install of updates

sideEffects: Microsoft Store apps — including WebView2-based and security-relevant apps such as the Windows Security helpers, Photos and Terminal — stop updating themselves and can go stale until you update them manually.

entries.title: Hide the organization name in update notifications
entries.description: On Microsoft Entra-joined devices, hides the organization name shown in Windows Update restart notifications.
entries.rationale: A cosmetic, reversible preference with no functional effect; harmless on devices that are not Entra-joined.

entries.title: Set active hours to 08:00-23:00
entries.description: Configures the Windows Update active-hours policy so automatic restarts do not happen between 08:00 and 23:00.
entries.rationale: A sensible default that keeps update restarts out of the working day and evening; the exact hours can be tuned later. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Turn off auto-restart for updates during active hours

entries.title: Quality-update restart deadline (7 days, 2-day grace)
entries.description: Requires security (quality) updates to install within 7 days of being offered, with a 2-day grace period, and does not force a restart while you are actively using the device before the deadline.
entries.rationale: Microsoft's recommended way to guarantee patching without surprise restarts: users control the restart until the deadline, after which the device restarts to stay secure.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Specify deadlines for automatic updates and restarts

sideEffects: After the 7-day deadline plus the 2-day grace period, the device will restart to finish a quality update even outside active hours, with a 15-minute warning.

entries.title: Feature-update restart deadline (7 days, 7-day grace)
entries.description: Requires feature updates to install within 7 days of being offered, with a 7-day grace period, and does not force a restart while you are actively using the device before the deadline.
entries.rationale: Applies the same deadline discipline to feature updates as to quality updates, with a longer grace period appropriate to the larger, less frequent feature update.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Specify deadlines for automatic updates and restarts

sideEffects: After the 7-day deadline plus the 7-day grace period, the device will restart to finish a feature update even outside active hours, with a 15-minute warning.

entries.title: Hide update notifications except restart warnings
entries.description: Sets the update notification level so Windows hides update notifications but still warns before a required restart.
entries.rationale: Reduces update noise while keeping the one notification that matters — the restart warning — so a restart is never a complete surprise.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Display options for update notifications

entries.title: Let me choose optional and preview updates
entries.description: Enables the 'Get the latest updates as soon as they're available' toggle and leaves the choice of optional and preview updates to you (AllowOptionalContent = 3).
entries.rationale: On policy-managed devices optional updates are otherwise hidden; this restores user choice without forcing early rollouts on.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage updates offered from Windows Update\Enable optional updates

entries.title: Get updates for other Microsoft products
entries.description: Registers the Microsoft Update service with Automatic Updates so security and quality updates for other Microsoft products (.NET, Office MSI, SQL Server, Visual Studio) arrive through Windows Update.
entries.rationale: Broadens patch coverage beyond the OS to the rest of the installed Microsoft stack, a security win; the same as the Settings toggle 'Receive updates for other Microsoft products'. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education; the Settings toggle and the WUA API work on Home too.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Configure Automatic Updates (Install updates for other Microsoft products)

sideEffects: Turning this off later stops security updates for .NET, Office MSI and other Microsoft products from arriving through Windows Update.

entries.title: Allow an 18-hour active-hours range
entries.description: Raises the maximum active-hours range to 18 hours so a wider working window can be protected from automatic update restarts.
entries.rationale: By default Windows caps the active-hours span; this policy allows the full 18-hour maximum, useful alongside an active-hours policy on machines used across a long day. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Specify active hours range for auto-restarts

sideEffects: Only takes effect alongside an active-hours policy, and has no effect if 'No auto-restart with logged on users' or 'Always automatically restart at the scheduled time' is set.

entries.title: Auto-download and schedule daily install
entries.description: Configures Automatic Updates to download updates automatically and install them on a daily schedule (03:00), rather than waiting for you to trigger the install.
entries.rationale: Keeps the machine reliably patched without manual intervention while confining installs to a chosen time; the scheduled alternative to notify-before-install. Documented Pro/Enterprise/Education.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Update\Manage end user experience\Configure Automatic Updates

sideEffects: Updates install and can restart automatically on the schedule; pair with active hours or a compliance deadline to keep restarts out of the working day.
